item.title: : AI Acceleration of Muon Collider R&D: A Report from the AI4MuC Workshop
item.description:
This is your report, so I note only the citable numbers and positions.

  • Smart pixels: a quantized NN gives ~85% BIB rejection at 99% signal efficiency. SEU studies suggest targeted mitigation beats full TMR.
  • Generative BIB: flow and tabular-diffusion results are reported as marginals only. The azimuthal-cloning in current FLUKA samples is explicitly named as blocking event-level correlations.
  • Software: the 3.x release moves to Gaudi/Key4hep/EDM4hep with ACTS, plus CI physics validation.
  • Agents: agent success above 80% on an analysis-task benchmark (Watts) is cited.
  • Grand challenges: four are proposed: cooling segment, BIB, smart pixel, and agent validation report.
  • BIB challenge ordering: independent full-simulation BIB samples come before the generative-model challenge. That ordering constrains follow-ups to your BIB work.

item.title: : Neutrino Tridents and W-boson production at the Muon Collider
item.description:
The setup is a 10 TeV collider with MuColν, a 100 kg silicon active target 500 m downstream, giving about 2×10¹⁰ CC DIS events over 10 years.

Process (10 yr, Si) Events
Dimuon tridents 3.05×10⁵
All trident channels ~2×10⁶
On-shell W production (WBP) (6.4±6.0)×10⁴
WBP, hadronic W 4.3×10⁴
  • Threshold: E_ν > m_W²/2m_N ≈ 3.44 TeV, giving x_min ≈ 0.69–0.86 for 4–5 TeV neutrinos.
  • Payoff: WBP measures the photon PDF at very large x, where the theory uncertainty exceeds 100%.
  • BSM reach: constraints on (Δg_V, Δg_A) collapse to a thin ring through the SM, far beyond DUNE.

The jet tie-in: hadronic W→qq̄ appears as a two-prong fat jet. Isolating it needs LHC-style W-tagging (cited at 10²–10³ rejection) plus a soft-primary-lepton cut against CC DIS, which is ~10⁴ larger. This is an unexplored substructure use case in a pileup-free forward detector.

Caveats: - The BSM projection is statistics-only, with backgrounds assumed negligible and WBP assumed separable. - The sensitivity plot omits detector systematics and flux uncertainties. - The W-tagging performance is assumed, not simulated.

item.title: Neutrino trident process at a muon collider
item.dc:creator: Reinaldo Francener et al.
item.description:
Setup. The authors estimate trident rates in a forward neutrino detector (“MuColν”): - Detector: 10 kg of tungsten (R = 10 cm, L = 1.65 cm), sited 500 m downstream of the IP. - Beam: 5 TeV μ beams, with a tree-level decay spectrum. - Flux: N_ν = 5×10¹⁷ ν_μ per year plus an equal number of ν̄_e. This assumes about 10% acceptance of decays along the 500 m straight section. - Cross section: the Altmannshofer et al. full 2→4 generator (no equivalent-photon approximation), adapted to W with a Woods–Saxon form factor. Coherent and incoherent contributions are both included.

Rates (before cuts, per year).

Final state Events
e⁺e⁻ ~1.0×10⁴
μ⁺μ⁻ 5.85×10³
τ⁺τ⁻ ~260
e±μ∓ 2.3×10⁴

Mixed-flavour channels are enhanced because only the W diagram contributes, so there is no destructive W/Z interference. Coherent scattering dominates (Z² scaling).

After cuts. Applying the FASER-style μμ cuts of Altmannshofer et al. [28] leaves about 3500 μμ events per year. The survival fractions are about 64% (coherent), 19% (incoherent p) and 48% (incoherent n).

BSM reach (Δg_V, Δg_A). - The 95% CL contours greatly tighten the CCFR ring, whether statistics-only or with 5% systematics. - For L_μ−L_τ Z′, the projections open new parameter space near m_Z′ ≈ 4 GeV and above the electroweak scale. - A 10-ton detector is claimed to reach g′ ~ 10⁻⁴ for m_Z′ ≳ 10⁻² GeV.

What this adds to the muon collider topic. It contributes another entry to the emerging forward-ν physics case, alongside Marzocca et al., Adhikary et al., and Kling et al. Its distinctive argument is that the clean, calculable flux makes a percent-level trident measurement plausible.

Caveats. - Backgrounds are not studied for this environment. Background rejection is borrowed from the LHC analysis; muon-collider beam-induced and halo backgrounds at the forward site are not discussed. - Flux treatment is idealized. The flux uncertainty is only tree level, and the beam divergence (0.6 mrad) enters just through the acceptance estimate. - Statistical framing is inconsistent. The Fig. 4 caption mixes “95% CL” with “±1σ.” - The 10-ton projection is statistics-only.

item.title: Input to the SCAC Facilities Subcommittee from the U.S. Muon Collider Collaboration (S. Jindariani (on behalf of the US Muon Collider Collaboration) et al.)
item.description:
This is a policy and strategy input to DOE’s SCAC with no new technical results. It asks SCAC to recognize muon-collider R&D as a gap in the 2026–2036 facilities portfolio and proposes a staged program: 1. Distributed micro-demonstrators covering HTS solenoids, RF in strong magnetic fields, high-power targets, fast-ramping magnets and power systems, detector timing, and integrated cooling-cell prototypes. 2. Parallel design of a macro-demonstrator. This is now framed as a higher-intensity front-end facility (proton driver, target and capture, production and cooling) with its own neutrino, dark-sector, flavor and nuclear physics program, rather than the earlier cooling-cell-only concept.

Other points relevant to tracking the program: - Cooling is restated as the dominant luminosity risk. MICE and g−2 demonstrated the principle, but a practical six-dimensional channel (~10⁶ phase-space reduction) with adequate transmission has not been shown. - The document states there is no dedicated DOE funding; current support comes from universities and private foundations (Simons, RCSA, Sloan). - It cites the 2026 ESPP explicit call for cooperation with the U.S. initiative. - It names AI4MuC target areas: cooling-channel optimization and beam-induced-background simulation.

There are no cost or schedule figures; the collaboration says the demonstrator is not yet mature enough for them.

item.title: The LHC is not enough: the LZ High-Recoil Event at FCC-hh and a Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Benedikt Maier et al.
item.description:
Maier and Spannowsky take the LZ 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate (2.6σ global) as motivation for a class of collider targets: pure Y≠0 electroweak multiplets with endothermic Z-mediated scattering and sub-2m_e neutral splitting. That splitting makes the neutral transitions invisible. Thermal masses run from 0.58 TeV (scalar doublet) to 11.5 TeV (scalar quintuplet). Within the leading-operator EFT, a charged-state trace sum rule caps Δ_min≲0.17 GeV for the quadruplets and quintuplets, which implies cτ≳18–27 mm. Most of the new quantitative work is FCC-hh: a disappearing-track rescaling model, plus monojet and Drell–Yan arguments. The muon-collider section is a compilation of published reaches (mainly Refs. [29, 32, 67]) mapped onto this benchmark set. There is no new muon-collider simulation.

The muon-collider case, as mapped here: - Why it suits these targets: lifetime-independent mono-γ/mono-W recoil searches. Disappearing-track reach approaches √(s)/2 for long-lived states but only ~0.3√(s) for the mm-scale doublet. Beam-induced-background-inclusive disappearing- and long-track studies cover the thermal Higgsino and wino at 10 TeV. - Coverage table: - fermion doublet: ≥3 TeV - scalar doublet: 6 TeV (disappearing tracks) - fermion triplet: ≥10 TeV - scalar triplet: 14 TeV (missing invariant mass; needs sub-percent systematics) - fermion quadruplet: ≥14 TeV (recoil channel needs sub-percent systematics, otherwise tracks) - fermion quintuplet: ≳20 TeV - scalar quintuplet: not reached at 30 TeV - Headline: 30 TeV covers the full fermionic family.

The useful framing is that recoil channels settle the doublet and triplet without knowing the charged spectrum, which is unpredicted once custodial-breaking operators are allowed.

Caveats: - Recoil projections assume 0–1‰ systematics, with 1% quoted only where it changes the conclusion. - The HTML I received truncates mid-§VI, so the detailed muon-collider discussion and caveats section were not available. - The authors themselves note that a full-density thermal Higgsino is in tension with solar-capture limits (δm_0≳0.51 MeV) and with the empty LZ high-energy sideband.

item.title: Spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration and muon mean lifetime
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Gallego Torrom\'e
item.description:
Tangential match — this is a classical-geometry theory paper, and “muon collider” enters only as a proposed testing ground. The claim: in a spacetime with a maximal proper acceleration A_max, the proper-time functional acquires a factor (1-a²/A_max²⁾¹/2, reducing the muon lifetime by Δ≈-12 a²/A_max². Given the measured lifetime precision (∼10⁻⁸), an observable effect requires 12 a²/A_max² ≳10⁻⁸.

Among the A_max candidates, only identifying A_max with the muon Schwinger acceleration A_S[μ]∼10²⁷ m/s² gives a testable window: a 10⁴ GeV circular muon collider with R∼10⁴ m yields proper acceleration a∼10²³ m/s², hence a ∼10⁻⁸ lifetime shift. High-order-jet electrodynamics (A_max∼8×10³⁴) and Caianiello (∼10³¹) give far-too-small effects. Caveats are self-flagged and severe: the Schwinger identification is a heuristic effective model, sits exactly at the acceleration scale where the classical geometric framework breaks down, and the whole construction presumes a well-defined classical worldline for the muon. Of no practical relevance to muon collider design or accelerator physics — file under exotic-physics phenomenology that happens to name-check the machine.

item.title: Thermomechanical rf breakdown from magnetically focused field emission in high-gradient normal-conducting cavities
item.dc:creator: Dillon Merenich et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon-collider) — original abstract; no AI summary.

Normal-conducting radiofrequency (rf) cavities for muon-collider ionization cooling must operate at high accelerating gradients in strong solenoidal magnetic fields, where rf breakdown can be enhanced by the magnetic focusing of field-emitted electrons. In this work, field-emitted electrons were tracked in the realistic field maps of rectilinear cooling-lattice cavities to test the validity of the previously developed localized-bombardment picture with simplified field maps. Under comparable reduced-field assumptions, the tracking results show good agreement with previous results. The full rf eigenmode fields and nonuniform solenoidal fields modify the idealized beamlet structure, producing rf phase dependent centroid shifts and broadened impact distributions from solenoid fringe fields. Nevertheless, the original model remains a useful framework for estimating limits on operating gradients. The thermal response is evaluated analytically using this model, with material properties varied to assess the coupled effects of heat transport and thermomechanical damage threshold. These results can inform cavity testing in strong solenoidal fields, muon ionization cooling channel designs, and other applications requiring high-gradient rf operation in magnetic fields.

item.title: Impedance of multilayer cylindrical structures with a material-filled beam region
item.dc:creator: Erik Kvikne et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — original abstract; no AI summary.

Beam-coupling impedances in material media are relevant for ionization-cooling channels of a future muon collider, where the beam propagates in matter rather than vacuum. We extend the cylindrical field-matching formalism for multilayer structures to the case of a material-filled beam region surrounded by external layers with arbitrary electromagnetic properties. Relative to the vacuum formulation, the usual factor 1/γ² is replaced by the material-dependent factor F=1/ε_1-μ_1β², and the radial propagation constant is modified accordingly. Analytical expressions are obtained for the monopolar longitudinal and dipolar transverse impedances, with the surrounding structure encoded through reflection coefficients determined by field matching. The formalism reduces to the known vacuum and perfectly conducting limits in the appropriate cases. Representative calculations are presented for absorber-relevant configurations, illustrating the dependence on the material properties of both the beam region and the surrounding layers. In particular, a finite beam-region conductivity can generate a real impedance component and reverse the sign of the imaginary space-charge impedance, while sufficiently high permittivity can give rise to resonant structures associated with oscillatory radial fields. The effect of finite-conductivity surroundings is also examined, showing the approach towards the perfectly conducting limit as the external conductivity is increased. The applicability of the infinite-length approximation is also discussed by comparison with finite-length mode-matching results.

item.title: Fast BIB simulation at a future Muon Collider with generative machine learning
item.dc:creator: Radha Mastandrea et al.
item.description:
First generative-ML surrogate for beam-induced-background hits in the tracking detectors of a 10 TeV muon collider (MAIA concept), targeting the FLUKA+Geant4 bottleneck (~10⁶ HS23·hr for the ~10% bunch-crossing sample currently used for overlay, ~100 GB/beam). They train per-subdetector (6 subdetectors) models that generate the five continuous hit observables (log E, t, r, φ, z) conditioned on cell-ID indices (side, layer, module, sensor), in a local-φ basis, followed by geometry masking/rejection and KD-tree cell-ID assignment. Two architectures: a TabDDPM-based tabular diffusion model (higher fidelity, slow sampling: 6–36 hr/subdetector) and a neural circular spline flow (lower fidelity, <2 min/subdetector). Both beat full sim by >1 order of magnitude in generation time.

Validation is thorough: hit-level marginals agree well (both struggle with log E details — diffusion misses the Geant4 1e-6 GeV cutoff peak, flow overshoots high-E tail); BDT classifier AUCs ~0.52–0.56 for diffusion, up to 0.61 for two flow barrel models; after ACTS CKF reconstruction, Loose-track counts match to ~3% (1.07M vs 1.03M) and hits-per-track distributions are nearly identical. r (barrel) and z (endcap) are the hardest features, localized to sensor boundaries.

Central caveat, stated plainly: only one “unique” training event exists — itself just 10% of a real BIB event replicated via 42 rigid azimuthal rotations — so inter-event correlations cannot be modeled or validated, and the 42 copies aren’t statistically independent. Weights/code/data are released; authors flag calorimeter and post-digitization generation as follow-ups.

item.title: Connecting Vector-like Muons, pNGB Dark Matter and Electroweak Phase Transition through Collider and Gravitational Wave
item.dc:creator: Jaydeb Das et al.
item.description:
The muon-collider content (Sec. 3) is genuinely central, not incidental. The model adds two complex singlets (Z₂, Z₃) plus a muon-philic SU(2) singlet vector-like lepton ψ sharing the Z₃ charge of S₃, so the only renormalizable new Yukawa is ψ̄_L μ’_R S₃. The stable pNGB η₂ (from S₂) is DM; η₃ decays to muons. For a multi-TeV μ⁺μ⁻ collider they argue the discovery channel is VLM pair production μ⁺μ⁻→vl⁺vl⁻, since associated production is suppressed by tanθ_L = (m_μ/m_vl)tanθ_R. The novel handle is the scalar-mediated t-channel (via h₃, η₃), which does not carry the sinθ_L suppression and, for sinθ_R=0.3, dominates the gauge s-channel by orders of magnitude; there is visible destructive interference with γ/Z for sinθ_R=0.1. LO cross sections (m_vl=1.4 TeV) reach 17.3 fb at 3 TeV (BP9) vs ~2.2 fb at 10 TeV — the 3 TeV rate is larger because the t-channel grows with m_vl despite phase-space loss.

The collider study is a full Delphes + XGBoost BDT analysis of the 2-opposite-sign-muon + E̸_T signature (vl→μh₃, h₃→η₂η₂), with seven observables (M_eff, L_T, ΔR_μμ, p_T^{l1}, E̸_T, M_μμ, M_T^{μμ}), a jet veto, and dominant irreducible background μ⁺μ⁻→μ⁺μ⁻ν ν̄. They quote test AUC = 0.982 and, at D_BDT>0.924 with 500 fb⁻¹, statistical significance Z∼12 for BP9. Caveat stated explicitly: Z is purely statistical, no background systematics; Δa_μ from the new states remains negligible across their benchmarks, so no g−2 tension or motivation is claimed.

item.title: Prospects for precision Higgs boson measurements at a 10 TeV muon collider
item.dc:creator: Paolo Andreetto et al.
item.description:
Full detector-level projections (MUSIC concept, GEANT4 + machine-induced BIB/IPP overlay, ACTS + Pandora PF, kt R=0.5 jets) for the IMCC baseline: two experiments × 10 ab⁻¹ (20 ab⁻¹ total), VBF-dominated production (~2×10⁷ single-H, 7×10⁴ HH). Headline statistical sensitivities on effective cross sections: H→bb̄ 0.18%, H→WW* (semileptonic) 0.35%, H→γγ 2.6%, H→ZZ*→qqμμ 4.2%, H→μμ 6.9%. Combining bb̄/γγ/μμ mass fits gives Δm_H ≈ 19 MeV (competitive with HL-LHC’s ~21 MeV). Double-Higgs: HH→bbbb at 4.2%, HH→bbWW* at 14%, translating to a projected ~5% precision on the trilinear self-coupling λ₃ from bbbb — the standout number, since HL-LHC is stuck at [−26%,+29%] on κ₃.

For this topic the paper is the current reference benchmark: it moves the μC Higgs case from parton-level cross-section studies to full reconstruction with realistic BIB, and gives channel-by-channel efficiencies (e.g. 60% b-tag with 22% c / 0.9% light mistag) and background models one can actually reuse. Key caveats stated openly: all quoted numbers are statistical only, and H→bb̄ will be JES-dominated (0.49% from a 0.06% JES uncertainty) once systematics enter; electron reconstruction is not yet optimized, so H→ZZ*→4ℓ and the electron HH→bbWW channel (53% vs 22% for muons) are deferred/conservative; τ_had reconstruction is absent. The λ₃ extraction relies solely on bbbb and on the WW-fusion sample rescaled by 1.103 for ZZ-fusion.

item.title: Probing the Inert Scalar Sector of the Inert Doublet Model via Vector-Boson Fusion at a Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Abdesslam Arhrib et al.
item.description:
Studies three previously-unexamined 2→4 VBF channels in the IDM at √s = 3, 10, 20 TeV: μ⁺μ⁻→H⁺H⁻νν̄ (WW fusion), and the associated HH±μ∓ν and AH±μ∓ν (WZ/Wγ fusion), with full 2→4 matrix elements in MadGraph5 (no EVBA). They first dissect the WW→H⁺H⁻ and WV→H⁺S_i subprocesses, showing longitudinal WLWL dominance and a strong destructive interference among diagrams (individual contributions ~10³ pb collapse to ~1 pb in the full amplitude), enforcing correct high-energy behavior. Cross sections rise sharply with energy: H⁺H⁻νν̄ reaches O(10) fb at 10 TeV and tens of fb at 20 TeV; the associated channels reach O(10³) fb. Delphes-level cut-based analysis (no BIB/pileup) for three benchmark points with BR(H±→HW±)=1 gives, at 10 ab⁻¹: [WH][WH]νν̄ significance 33 (10 TeV) / 58 (20 TeV); [WH]Hμν a huge 2000–4000 (dominated by large signal σ); [WH][ZH]μν 164 / 276. The 3 TeV stage is marginal for H⁺H⁻ (S=1.37) but strong for the associated modes.

For the muon-collider topic this extends the VBF new-physics program beyond the earlier AAνν̄ study to charged and mixed inert states, establishing 10/20 TeV as decisive. Caveat, stated by the authors: this is an idealized sensitivity — pileup and MuC beam-induced background are not simulated, and the enormous significances (especially BP2) reflect raw signal rates under optimistic detector assumptions rather than a realistic backgrounded analysis.

item.title: Light Leptoquarks in a Dark Sector: Scalar Dark Matter, Neutrino Mass, and Collider Signatures
item.dc:creator: Priyotosh Bandyopadhyay et al.
item.description:
The muon collider is genuinely only the final probe in an otherwise DM/neutrino-mass model paper, so calibrate expectations: Sections 2–4 build a Z₂-odd dark sector (two scalar LQs S₁ and R̃₂, a VLQ doublet + down-type singlet, and a real singlet scalar φ as DM), generate Majorana neutrino mass at one loop via the T1-2 topology (requiring κ~10⁻³ GeV for TeV masses and O(10⁻²–1) Yukawas), and satisfy relic density through LQ–φ co-annihilation with compressed splittings ΔM~38–55 GeV. The Z₂-odd assignment kills the usual ℓq/νq LQ decays, so LHC pair-production bounds drop from ~1.5 TeV to a few hundred GeV; CheckMATE recasts of soft-lepton (CMS-SUS-16-048) and jets+MET searches leave sub-TeV LQ eigenstates viable for M_φ ≳ 500 GeV.

The muon-collider content (Sec. 5) is the motivated but not-yet-executed part: they argue a 10 TeV MuC is the right machine to measure the compressed S₁→ℓqφ system because M_T2 fails when invisible daughters aren’t light relative to the parent, whereas the known √s lets you use visible-energy endpoints and the cusp technique. They set up the two-body-like kinematics S₁→V+φ with V=jℓ, giving the Lorentz-invariant endpoint m_jℓ^max = M_{S₁}−M_φ = ΔM as a robust handle on the splitting. Caveat: no signal-vs-background simulation, detector effects, or cusp-fit sensitivity study is actually presented — the MuC analysis is a proposal/kinematic sketch, and displaced-vertex R-hadron-like regions are explicitly excluded from scope. For MuC-tracking purposes, the takeaway is a concrete use-case for endpoint/cusp reconstruction of compressed colored-parent spectra at 10 TeV, not a new reach result.

item.title: An Axial U_A(1)_L_μ-L_τ: UV Completion and Experimental Searches
item.dc:creator: Rundong Fang et al.
item.description:
Be aware up front: this is primarily an intensity-frontier / UV-completion paper. The muon collider appears only in Sec. IV as one of several complementary probes; the bulk is trident production, muon beam dumps, invisible meson decays, (g-2)_μ, and four-muon resonance recasts for a purely axial L_μ-L_τ gauge boson (axial charged-lepton current, LH neutrino current, masses via a universal-seesaw with M_E>10 TeV vector-like leptons). Under their benchmark (Q_ℓ=1, y_μτ=0, θ≤10⁻², scalar decoupled m_s≳10 GeV) the phenomenology collapses to (m_A’,g_X) with v_s=m_A’/2g_X.

The collider-relevant point: for FSR-type observables (e⁺e⁻,Z→μ⁺μ⁻A’, and muon-collider radiative return μ⁺μ⁻→γA’) the vector/axial difference is only the longitudinal mode, ∝m_μ²/m_A’², so for m_A’≫m_μ axial limits are obtained by simple branching-ratio rescaling of published vector limits — total rate does not discriminate chirality. Their proposed discriminator is the two-body μ⁺μ⁻→τ⁺τ⁻ (s-channel γ/Z/A’ only) angular distribution at √(s)=3 TeV. Using massless-external-lepton chiral amplitudes (Eq. 65–66, chiral couplings in Table 3), for m_A’=1 TeV, g_X=0.05: the vector case shifts the |cosθ|<0.9 rate by ~5% vs ~2% axial, but the axial case shifts A_FB by ΔA_FB≃-2.9×10⁻², exceeding the vector shift. So A_FB retains direct sensitivity to the axial current where rates wash it out.

Caveat, stated explicitly: no detector-level Monte Carlo; they use Γ_A’=g_X² m_A’/4π and analytic amplitudes, and defer a real exclusion to a follow-up modeled on Ref. [62]. This is a “here is a viable observable” argument, not a sensitivity contour.

item.title: On-Detector Machine Learning for Beam-Induced Background Rejection at a 10 TeV Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Daniel Abadjiev et al.
item.description:
This is the smart-pixels concept ported from HL-LHC to the muon collider BIB problem, and it’s squarely on-topic for detector R&D at √s = 10 TeV. The concrete driver: innermost vertex layer occupancy of O(10⁴) hits/cm²/BX at 30 kHz translates to >50 Gbps/chip (2×2 cm², 40-bit hits) — ~10× the HL-LHC pixel readout ceiling. The pitch is to reject BIB in the pixel front-end using cluster shape rather than relying solely on O(30) ps timing, which they argue is fragile at 25×25 µm² pitch (needs ~10× front-end power reduction) and vulnerable to calibration/radiation drift. Physics handle: collision particles hit at IP-consistent incidence angles (x_size grows with z_global), whereas BIB e± loop in at large angles regardless of position, giving distinct cluster sizes/profiles.

They train three quantized NN classes — engineered scalars (Model 1), 1D charge profiles (Model 2), full 21×13 CNN (Model 3) — via QKeras QAT, Pareto-scanned over architecture and 3–10 bit weights, with hls4ml→Vitis (FPGA) and Catapult/SAED32 (32 nm ASIC) resource estimates. Headline: 88–90% data reduction at 99% signal efficiency for Models 1–2 with ASIC area <1 mm² and 160–250 ns latency; Model 3 reaches 90.5% cluster rejection / 94.4% data reduction but at prohibitive area (~8 mm²). Crucially, cluster-shape rejection is shown orthogonal to timing — BIB is rejected across the full t_corr spectrum, and stacking a [3σ,5σ] window pushes data reduction to 98.5–98.9%.

Caveats are stated plainly and are significant: PIXELAV assumes a single isolated cluster in a clean ROI (no overlapping/warped BIB clusters, no edge effects, ROI-finding assumed upstream) — unrealistic at true muon-collider occupancy. Incoherent pair production is absent from the BIB sample (they argue IPP clusters look similar and should be rejectable if trained on). Signal is single muons, not physics events; geometry is MuColl_v1 / lattice v0.4; ASIC numbers are open-library first-pass, not manufacturable. So: a credible feasibility demonstration and benchmark (88–90% @ 99% eff, sub-mm² ASIC), not yet a validated occupancy-realistic result.

item.title: Probing the ALP–Photon–Dark Photon Interaction through the Mono-Photon plus Missing-Energy Signature at a Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Chong-Xing Yue et al.
item.description:
A detector-level (MadGraph5+Pythia8+Delphes generic MC card) study of the dark axion portal coupling g_aγγ’ via μ⁺μ⁻→aγ’, a→γγ’ at √(s)=1.5 TeV, ℒ=500 fb⁻¹, assuming m_a≫m_γ’ so both dark photons escape and the signal is mono-photon + MET. Production runs through s-channel γ and Z, with the EW-gauge-invariance relation g_aZγ’=-tanθ_W g_aγγ’. The dominant background is μ⁺μ⁻→νν̅γ, whose radiative-return peak (E_γ≈750 GeV, Z→νν̅ on-shell) is killed by cuts on MET, |η_γ|<1.2, and recoil mass. Projected 2σ reach spans g_aγγ’∼1.7×10⁻⁵–9.1×10⁻⁵ GeV⁻¹ over 1≤m_a≤1200 GeV for the fully polarized P(μ⁺,μ⁻⁾⁼⁽⁻¹⁰⁰%,+100%) beam, and ∼1.0×10⁻⁴–4.5×10⁻⁴ GeV⁻¹ unpolarized.

For the muon-collider topic this is a first look at the dark axion portal at a muon machine (previously only e⁺e⁻/hadron colliders), and its distinctive contribution is reach in ALP mass up to ∼1.2 TeV — well beyond the 𝒪(10–80) GeV windows of LEP/BaBar and the m_a≲50 GeV coverage of the FCC-ee projection. That said, in raw coupling sensitivity it is outperformed everywhere by FCC-ee (10⁻⁶–10⁻⁷), STCF (10⁻⁶), and Belle II/BESIII (10⁻⁵); the value claimed is complementarity via high-mass coverage, not depth.

Two visible caveats blunt the headline. The strong (10⁻⁵) numbers rely on ideal ±100% beam polarization, which the authors concede is unrealistic; the unpolarized significances collapse to SS=1.8→0.35 across m_a=100→1000 GeV, i.e. below 2σ over much of the range. Prompt a decay is assumed throughout — a long-lived/displaced treatment (left to future work) would change both signal efficiency and background.

item.title: RF cavity design and beam loading effects in the rectilinear cooling channel for a muon collider
item.dc:creator: C. Barbagallo et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — original abstract; no AI summary.

High-gradient normal-conducting RF cavities are crucial components of the rectilinear cooling channel in a muon collider, providing the accelerating field necessary to sustain the rapid six-dimensional ionization cooling essential to achieve high luminosity. To reach this goal, a muon collider requires approximately 10¹² muons per bunch. At such high beam intensities, beam loading induced by bunch-driven wakefields can significantly reduce the cavity accelerating gradient and compromise beam stability. This paper focuses on the conceptual RF design and beam-induced effect analysis of copper cavities with so-called beam windows developed to meet the beam dynamics requirements of the rectilinear muon cooling channel. We first present the design and optimization of the cavities, evaluating their RF performance and power requirements. Thereafter, we analyze cavity wakefields and beam loading effects, proposing a new numerical method for their compensation, which takes the transverse distribution of the beam into account.

item.title: Production of the top partner T of the Bestest Little Higgs Model at the future muon collider
item.dc:creator: E. Cruz-Albaro et al.
item.description:
Abstract only. A BLHM phenomenology study computing decay widths and branching ratios of the heavy top partner T and its production at a μ⁺μ⁻ collider through both pair production, μ⁺μ⁻→(γ,Z,Z’,h,H)→TT̅, and single/associated production, μ⁺μ⁻→(γ,Z,Z’,h,H)→t̅ T + tT̅. Cross sections are scanned over several √(s) values; the headline conclusion is that pair production is the most promising discovery channel. No numbers, mass points, or luminosity/reach figures are given in the abstract.

For the muon-collider track this is a standard added-physics-case exercise rather than a machine or analysis advance: the novelty is applying the s-channel neutral-current mediator set (including the BLHM-specific Z’, h, H) to top-partner production, but the abstract offers no sensitivity benchmark or comparison against hadron-collider limits. Judge relevance once the full text provides the actual σ(√(s)) curves and the assumed T mass range relative to the Z’/H resonance thresholds — the associated tT channel is the more collider-specific observable and worth checking whether it stays subdominant across all √(s) or only near threshold.

item.title: Neutrino Fluxes at a Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Francis M. Burk et al.
item.description:
Comprehensive re-evaluation of all neutrino sources for the v0.8 IR design. Key number: beam-muon-decay flux is ~10¹⁹ ν/year in the forward direction, ~120× higher than the ISU/IMCC estimate, driven by integrating over the full ~500 m straight section (not just 10 m) and increasing collimation away from the IP. They also quantify three previously-neglected subdominant sources: (i) primary μ⁺μ⁻ collisions, dominated by γγ→τ⁺τ⁻ (~0.4–1 nb, ~10¹⁰ ν_τ at 10 ab⁻¹, cross-checked between DGLAP-resummed PDFs and fixed-order WHIZARD to O(10%)); (ii) Michel-electron EM showers in the tungsten shielding, where Bethe–Heitler γN→τ⁺τ⁻/cc̄ and photo-nuclear γg→cc̄ give ~10¹² ν/year of all flavors — this is the leading source of ν_τ; (iii) ν-induced showers in rock (~10¹¹/year). For a 100 kg MuColν detector at z=500 m, r=25 cm (0.5 mrad acceptance, >80% acceptance for beam-decay ν), Table 1 gives 1.1·10¹⁰ ν_μ + 5.2·10⁹ ν̄_e per 10 yr, but only ~2.5 ν_τ+ν̄_τ events total. Physics case: 10¹⁰ DIS/ton/yr enables PDF/CKM (V_cd ×44, V_ub ×3), sin²θ_W to 0.03%, ν trident, NSI improved ~10× over their earlier projection, sterile Δm²~10³ eV².

Caveat, stated explicitly: absolute flux carries an O(1) machine-design uncertainty — v0.6 vs v0.8 differ by ~2–5× depending on chicane treatment. The tiny ν_τ yield is the weak point of the physics case at this detector size.

item.title: The Forward Neutrino Flux and its Secondaries at a 10 TeV Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Ju-Yeol Choi et al.
item.description:
Introduces MINT, a public MC that propagates the central muon orbit through a MAD-X hybrid v0.6+v0.9 lattice including Twiss-based beam envelope and divergence (though not full particle tracking). Central result that qualitatively updates prior work: the beam divergence (O(0.1–1) mrad over the straight section) is ~50× larger than the intrinsic 1/γ≈0.02 mrad, so the energy–angle “prism” correlation touted in preliminary studies is washed out — recovering it would require β increasing ~100×. Benchmark: 3.2 t fiducial (gas Ar TPC + vertex tracker) at 5 km, ~60% acceptance, ~7·10¹⁸ ν/year crossing the face, O(10⁹) interactions/year.

Their distinctive contribution is the secondary flux from ν interactions in the upstream rock. Secondary muons: 6.5·10¹²/yr (μ⁺ beam) and 1.2·10¹³/yr (μ⁻) produced in the last 2.5 km, ~6·10¹¹/yr reaching the face at ⟨E_μ⟩≈1.2 TeV — ~2 muons per bunch crossing, ~40–45× the neutrino interaction rate, a serious background requiring event-by-event (not per-bunch) vetoing, and >99.9% polarized (potential feature). Secondary ν_τ: charm→D_s→τ dominates but only ~0.2 events/year total (peaks near L=3 km) — consistent with 2714’s conclusion that ν_τ are scarce, and they note photoproduction in the ring (2714’s channel) likely dominates. Wrong-sign ν: O(4)/yr (μ⁻), O(0.7)/yr (μ⁺). BSM section estimates HNL reach (mixing |U_μN|²~2·10⁻¹¹ at m_N≈15 GeV; dipole d~4·10⁻¹⁰ GeV⁻¹ at m_N≈6 GeV) via ν upscattering, exploiting √s≈75 GeV(E_ν/3TeV)^½ to exceed D/B-meson kinematic ceilings.

Caveat, emphasized by the authors: HNL curves are event-yield contours before backgrounds/efficiencies, not sensitivity projections; the secondary-muon background and vertexing/timing requirements are the gating issues. MINT omits individual optics tracking.

Net for the topic: the ~120× flux upward revision (2714) and the demonstration that beam dynamics, not 1/γ, sets the beam profile and kills the prism effect (2718) together reset the design assumptions. Both agree ν_τ are rare (~0.2–2.5 events), tempering the “tau factory” framing; the real leverage is the ~10⁹–10¹⁰ ν_μ/ν_e CC sample and the secondary-muon background now quantified for the first time.

item.title: Probing Lepton-Flavor-Violating Four-Lepton Operators at a Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Sukanta Dutta et al.
item.description:
Abstract only. A SMEFT study of charged LFV from dimension-six four-lepton operators in μ⁺μ⁻→e^±τ^∓, e^±μ^∓, μ^±τ^∓ at √(s)=3,10,14 TeV, with beam polarization and hadronic τ reconstruction. Using an optimal-observable analysis of angular distributions and a global fit over the relevant operator set, they project sensitivities of C/Λ²∼(0.6–1.6)×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻², up to an order of magnitude beyond current limits. The multi-energy, multi-polarization combination is highlighted as the lever that breaks correlations among Wilson coefficients — the concrete methodological point for anyone tracking how a muon collider’s LFV reach depends on running scenario.

For this topic the paper is squarely on-target: it’s a projection specific to a multi-TeV muon collider, exploiting the s-channel LFV production that only a muon-beam machine gives directly. Caveats limited by abstract-only: no statement of assumed integrated luminosity per energy point, no detail on the τ-reconstruction efficiency/background model behind the quoted reach, and the sensitivities are presumably from a truth- or fast-sim level fit rather than full detector simulation. The “exceeds current limits by an order of magnitude” claim should be read against which specific low-energy LFV constraint (e.g. μ→e, τ→ℓ) each operator direction is compared to.

item.title: Higgs Couplings at a Future Wakefield Collider
item.dc:creator: Katherine Fraser et al.
item.description:
Abstract only. The paper’s actual subject is 10 TeV wakefield colliders (e⁺e⁻, e⁻e⁻, γγ) and their Higgs coupling reach; the muon collider appears only as a benchmark for comparison, not as an object of study. The one relevant claim: a 10 ab⁻¹ γγ dataset yields “qualitatively similar sensitivity” to Higgs electroweak couplings as 10 ab⁻¹ at a muon collider (and to 1 ab⁻¹ at an e⁺e⁻ wakefield machine). So the muon collider here serves as the established high-energy reference point against which the wakefield alternatives are calibrated.

For your tracking purposes this is tangential — it does not present new muon-collider physics, detector, or luminosity work. The takeaway is external context: it positions the muon collider’s 10 ab⁻¹ Higgs program as roughly equivalent in coupling sensitivity to a γγ wakefield option that sidesteps positron acceleration, and an order of magnitude behind a clean e⁺e⁻ wakefield collider per unit luminosity. Caveat flagged in the abstract itself: the wakefield conclusions hinge on measuring/calculating the luminosity spectra to high accuracy, given the beam-beam interactions — a caveat that does not apply symmetrically to the muon-collider benchmark. No numbers on individual couplings are given in the abstract.

item.title: The muon collider: expected physics, technological solutions, and the prospect of a 21 km ring at the UNK site
item.dc:creator: L. V. Dudko
item.description:
Single-author review (Dudko) that is 90% a consolidation of the existing IMCC/MuCol case, with one genuinely new element: a site-specific proposal to reuse the excavated-but-never-equipped 20,772 m UNK tunnel at Protvino as a muon-collider ring. The physics and technology sections are a competent restatement of known numbers (MuCol reference parameters; 0.75% on σ(H→bb̄) at 3 TeV full-sim; Higgs width pinned to (−0.41%,+2.1%) at 10 TeV via forward-μ ZZ-fusion tagging with |η|<6; δλ₃ ~4% at 10 TeV, ~1–1.5% at 30 TeV; thermal wino covered with ~70 fb⁻¹, higgsino needing ~8 ab⁻¹; MICE transverse-cooling demonstration; HTS/REBCO magnet roadmap). Nothing new there — treat it as a reference index.

The novel content is Section 4. Using the rigidity relation with R≈3306 m and a dipole packing factor calibrated to the IMCC 10 TeV lattice (f≈0.66; as-built UNK-II gives f≈0.59), the author maps arc fields onto √s: conventional NbTi/Nb₃Sn (7–8.3 T) → ~8–11 TeV, HTS (10–16 T) → ~12–21 TeV. The one physically interesting argument is the luminosity scaling: at fixed √s, ℒ ∝ B̄ ∝ 1/C, so the 20.8 km ring delivers only ≈0.55× the 11.4 km reference luminosity at 10 TeV — a deficit that closes only by running the fixed ring at the top of its energy range (B̄≈10.5 T at 21 TeV).

Caveats are stated plainly by the author: no CDR exists, the entire front end (driver, target, 6D cooling, acceleration) must still be built (and dominates cost), the reach table is pure extrapolation of published curves at assumed design luminosity, and the neutrino-flux constraint worsens with energy — the 20–60 m tunnel depth is shallower than IMCC dose studies assume, with decay-plane neutrinos surfacing 16–28 km out in populated regions. Also flagged: institutional (CERN–Russia cooperation suspended, IMCC closed to Russian labs). Bottom line for this track: no new physics or accelerator result, but a concrete tunnel-reuse scenario and a clean 1/C luminosity argument worth noting alongside the LHC/SPS reuse options.

item.title: Multiboson Signatures of Doubly Charged Scalars at a Same-Sign Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Mariana Frank et al.
item.description:
Frank, Fuks, Majumdar & Senapati study a same-sign μ⁺μ⁺ collider (the μTRISTAN 2 TeV / 1 ab⁻¹ configuration) as a probe of Type-II seesaw doubly charged scalars in the large-triplet-vev regime (v_t ≃ 1 GeV), where Δ^{±±}→W^±W^± dominates (BR >90%) rather than the dilepton mode. Production is VBF-like pair production μ⁺μ⁺→μ⁺μ⁺Δ⁺⁺Δ⁻⁻ with two spectator muons, and they target the fully hadronic 4W channel giving a μ⁺μ⁺+8j final state (~20% combined hadronic BR). Combinatorics are resolved via a global χ² minimization over the 105 ways of forming four non-overlapping dijets from the 8 leading jets, with σ_W=12 GeV. Backgrounds (μ⁺μ⁺+2j/4j, μ⁺μ⁺W⁺W⁻) are driven to the ~1–8 ab level by the N_j≥8 requirement. A cut-and-count analysis with three nested “tight-W” regions gives 3.7–4.7σ for m_{Δ}=200–300 GeV, dropping below 2σ near 400 GeV — the fall driven by the steeply falling production cross section, not reconstruction. An XGBoost BDT (per-mass classifiers, kinematic + reconstructed-W + spectator-muon + multi-W-mass observables) extends the 2σ reach to 425–430 GeV, a few tens of GeV beyond the cut-based result.

For this topic, the concrete takeaway is a benchmark reach number for a genuinely same-sign (μ⁺μ⁺) machine in a decay regime where LHC diboson searches only reach ~350 GeV (pair) / ~230 GeV (associated) — so the improvement over LHC is modest but comes from a qualitatively different production mode and clean initial state. Caveats stated explicitly: no ME-to-PS matching/merging (backgrounds treated conservatively/independently), no beam-induced-background or dedicated detector study, and the LO Delphes treatment with a generic muon-collider card. The extra “missing-energy” BDT variables are acknowledged as event-balance proxies, not genuine invisible-particle handles. Overall the paper is fully and centrally about the muon-collider capability, not a tangential keyword match.

item.title: Probing Fermion-Portal Scalar Dark Matter through Charged Vector-Like Fermions at Future Muon Colliders
item.dc:creator: Songshaptak De et al.
item.description:
This study investigates a dark matter (DM) model featuring a real singlet scalar (s) and vector-like singlet/doublet charged fermions (E_S, F_D), where the DM is stabilized by a Z_2 symmetry. By introducing Yukawa interactions (Y_f), the authors successfully move away from the minimal Higgs-portal scenario, which is currently under extreme pressure from LZ direct-detection limits. The model reproduces the observed relic density via t- and u-channel processes (s s →νℓν̅ ℓ) and co-annihilations involving the new fermions.

The paper provides a detailed collider sensitivity analysis for the process μ⁺ μ⁻ →E_1⁺ E_1⁻ →e⁺ e⁻ + E_T. Using detector-level simulation (Delphes), the authors demonstrate that a 3 TeV muon collider (ℒ=1 ab⁻¹) can reach a 5σ discovery for charged fermion masses up to ∼1.5 TeV. Scaling to 10 TeV (ℒ=10 ab⁻¹) extends this reach to ∼2 TeV, covering almost the entire parameter space favored by current relic density and direct-detection constraints.

The results are significant because they highlight the complementarity of a muon collider in probing “compressed” or weakly-coupled regions that the HL-LHC cannot reach, specifically for Z_2-odd states. A notable caveat is the reliance on the electron channel; the muon-associated Yukawa couplings are intentionally suppressed to evade (g-2)_μ and μ→e γ constraints, which justifies the focus on electron-rich final states but constrains the model’s flavor structure.

item.title: Prospects for probing neutral vector-like leptons via pair production at muon collider
item.dc:creator: Chong-Xing Yue et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Vector-like leptons (VLLs) are well-motivated candidates for physics beyond the Standard Model. We investigate the sensitivity of the 6 TeV muon collider to the neutral doublet VLL (denoted as N) via its pair production within a general VLL framework. Taking vector-like muon as a case study, we study the subsequent decay N→W⁺ μ and analyze two representative signals, namely 4j2μ and 2ℓ2μE-10.5 mu/, arising from the hadronic and leptonic decays of the W boson, respectively. The signal and background events are simulated within a complete Monte Carlo framework, and a cut-based analysis is performed at the 6 TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity ℒ=4 ab⁻¹ and beam polarizations (P_μ⁺,P_μ⁻⁾⁼⁽⁻¹,1). We consider VLL masses in the range of 1300-3000 GeV and evaluate the corresponding search sensitivity. Our results show that the future 6 TeV muon collider can effectively probe neutral doublet VLLs through the 4j2μ and 2ℓ2μE-10.5 mu/ signals, with statistical significances exceeding 5σ over a broad mass range. These results demonstrate that the future 6 TeV muon collider has excellent potential to search neutral doublet VLLs.

item.title: Dispersion Suppression for Wedge-Based Final Cooling at a 10 TeV Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Inci Karaaslan et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Achieving a luminosity of ≳10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ in a 10 TeV Muon Collider, given the short lifetime of a muon, requires reducing the 6D emittance of the muon beam through a process known as ionization cooling. In the final stage of this cooling process, the transverse emittance must be reduced to 22 μm, typically by allowing longitudinal emittance growth up to downstream acceptance limits. While the current International Muon Collider Collaboration designs involve 40 T solenoids to reach the transverse emittance target, such high-field solenoids come with several challenges, including mechanical stress management, quench protection, and potential limitations in relying on High Temperature Superconductor technology. Designed as an alternative to using such solenoids while simultaneously reaching target transverse emittance, the previously proposed wedge-based, reverse emittance-exchange cooling scheme requires excellent dispersion suppression. In this study, we design and simulate a dispersion suppressor channel for the wedge-based final cooling design that reduces dispersion in the target direction to a target value of D_x ∼0.001 m.

item.title: Pair Production of Singlet Vector-Like B Quarks in Boosted bZ Final States at a Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Eda Alici
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider, muon-collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We investigate the pair production of singlet vector-like bottom quarks at a future 10 TeV muon collider in the boosted Zb final-state topology. The signal process is considered as μ⁺μ⁻→BB̅→(Zb)(Zb̅), with one Z boson decaying leptonically and the other hadronically, leading to a final state with an opposite-sign same-flavour dilepton pair, multiple jets, and two b-tagged jets. Signal and Standard Model background events are generated at leading order with MadGraph5_\allowbreak aMC@NLO and subsequently interfaced with \textsc{Pythia}~8 for parton showering and hadronization. Detector effects are simulated with \textsc{Delphes} using a muon-collider detector configuration. A cut-based analysis exploiting boosted kinematics, including hard leading-b-jet transverse momentum, small dilepton angular separation, and large hadronic activity, is performed to suppress the dominant ZZjj, ZZbb̅, and tt̅ backgrounds. Statistical sensitivities are evaluated with the Asimov approximation, including both zero and 10% background systematic uncertainty scenarios. For the singlet benchmark BR(B→bZ)=0.25 and an integrated luminosity of 10 ab⁻¹, a 5σ discovery reach up to M_B≃4.3 TeV is obtained, reduced slightly to M_B≃4.2 TeV when systematic effects are included. These results demonstrate that a 10 TeV muon collider provides a powerful and clean environment for probing vector-like B quarks well beyond present LHC limits.

item.title: New Avenues of Heavy Neutral Lepton at Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Fa-Xin Yang et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

With initial state radiation, the multi-TeV muon collider can be regarded as an electroweak boson collider. The dominant production mode of the certain process becomes the vector boson fusion channel, because the corresponding cross section typically increases logarithmically at high energies. This also holds true for new physics beyond the standard model. Within the U(1) gauged extension of seesaw models, the heavy neutral lepton has additional interactions with the new gauge boson Z’ and heavy Higgs H. In this paper, we investigate the production of heavy neutral lepton N via the new vector boson fusion processes Z’Z’→H→NN with and Z’Z’→NN without heavy Higgs at the multi-TeV muon collider. Different from the canonical vector boson fusion processes WW/ZZ→H→NN, the new process Z’Z’→H→NN is not suppressed by the small mixing angle α between the Higgs bosons. Meanwhile, the pair production process Z’Z’→NN is also viable even for heavy Higgs m_H> √(s). Therefore, these new avenues provide alternative pathways to probe the intrinsic feature of the heavy neutral lepton. We then perform a detailed analysis of the lepton number violation signals via the new vector boson fusion with heavy Higgs μ⁺μ⁻→μ⁺μ⁻ H →μ⁺μ⁻ NN and without heavy Higgs μ⁺μ⁻→μ⁺μ⁻ NN, followed by N→μ^±jj, where the two jets from W boson decay are treated as one fat-jet J.

item.title: Agentic Hybrid RAG for Evidence-Grounded Muon Collider Analysis
item.dc:creator: Ruobing Jiang et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Muon collider research spans accelerator physics, detector instrumentation, and high-energy phenomenology, with relevant evidence scattered across a rapidly expanding and heterogeneous body of scientific literature. As high-energy physics (HEP) increasingly explores agent-assisted analysis workflows, efficiently locating, integrating, and verifying scientific evidence becomes an essential capability. While retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offers a promising framework for scientific question answering, integrating agentic reasoning without compromising retrieval precision remains a key challenge. In this work, we present agentic hybrid RAG, an evidence-grounded RAG framework for muon collider research. The framework combines a hybrid retriever, integrating sparse lexical and dense semantic retrieval, with an agentic reasoning module for query decomposition, evidence expansion, and grounded answer generation. To enable systematic evaluation, we construct the first benchmark for retrieval-augmented scientific question answering in the muon collider domain, comprising a curated literature corpus together with dedicated retrieval and answer-generation benchmarks covering major detector and physics research topics. Extensive evaluation shows that hybrid retrieval provides the strongest retrieval backbone, while agentic reasoning is most effective for controlled evidence expansion and answer synthesis. Built on this principle, agentic hybrid RAG consistently outperforms representative retrieval and RAG baselines in retrieval effectiveness, answer quality, evidence coverage, and factual grounding. Together, the benchmark and framework provide a foundation for evidence-grounded scientific question answering and future HEP analysis agents operating over large-scale scientific literature.

item.title: Probing TeV-Scale Inverse-Seesaw Leptogenesis and Majorana Dark Matter in U(1)_B-L Models at Multi-TeV Muon Colliders
item.dc:creator: Xin-Qiang Li et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We investigate a predictive and testable framework in which dark matter (DM), heavy-neutrino dynamics, and the BAU originate from correlated interactions within a local U(1)_B-L extension of the SM. Unlike conventional B-L constructions based on the type-I seesaw, we employ an inverse-seesaw mechanism realized through a sterile fermion S_1 and a complex scalar field φ, whose vacuum expectation value simultaneously generates the masses of the heavy neutrinos N_1,2 and the Majorana DM fermion χ via Yukawa couplings. The small lepton-number-violating parameter induced by a higher-dimensional operator leads to naturally light active neutrinos together with TeV-scale heavy neutrinos and sizable active-sterile mixing, yielding distinctive collider signatures unavailable in minimal B-L models. The relic abundance of χ is governed by annihilation channels mediated by the same scalar and gauge interactions, producing a direct and model-specific correlation between successful leptogenesis and the observed DM relic density. A combined parameter-space analysis incorporating neutrino oscillation data, lepton-flavor-violating processes, direct-detection limits, and collider bounds on N_1,2 and Z^’ reveals a narrow yet robust region consistent with all these constraints. Representative benchmark points in this region are examined at a future multi-TeV muon collider. Heavy-neutrino production through electroweak processes yields striking signatures in the dilepton plus missing energy (2ℓ+ E/_T) and single-lepton plus di-jet plus missing energy (1ℓ+ 2j + E/_T) final states. These channels demonstrate that next-generation muon colliders offer a powerful and complementary probe of the inverse-seesaw origin of neutrino masses, the DM relic density, and the TeV-scale leptogenesis within such an extended U(1)_B-L framework.

item.title: Dark Z' at a Muon Collider: Radiative Return versus Vector Boson Fusion
item.dc:creator: Nicko Angelo Rabang et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

A secluded, massive Abelian gauge boson called a dark Z’ may interact with the Standard Model through kinetic mixing and mass mixing in the Higgs sector. We determine the sensitivity of a future high-energy muon collider to discover such a particle and determine its mixing parameters. We examine a dark Z’ with mass from 100 GeV up to the collider energy for a set of collider benchmarks up to 14 TeV. We show the discovery reach and compare to the current and proposed future colliders. A muon collider is sensitive to two complementary production modes: radiative return (muon fusion with an associated photon), and vector boson fusion of W bosons. An observable photon distinguishes these production modes and the relative rates of these processes allows one to determine the relative mixing. Soft and collinear photons in the radiative return diagram contribute to the same final state as vector boson fusion. We show that these relative rates alone can determine the mixing to an accuracy comparable to that of a fully polarized muon beam using a left-right asymmetry.

item.title: Muon-induced di-tau production as a probe of new physics
item.dc:creator: Sudipta Das et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

The muon trident process, which involves coherent scattering to produce tau pairs, is a powerful tool for constraining dark sectors. We propose to explore this channel using future high-energy muon beams with the dedicated active-target detector, High-Energy Muon Electronic Research Apparatus (HEMERA). The detector would complement muon beam-dump searches by resolving prompt signatures and could operate from preparatory facilities involving an individual muon beam of the full Muon Collider. We illustrate its capabilities for a leptophilic scalar with Yukawa-like couplings that can mediate thermal dark matter production. With 10¹⁸ incident TeV-scale muons, even a compact 10 kg silicon-based HEMERA will extend current B-factory and (g-2)_μ bounds by over an order of magnitude in coupling strength. In the leptophilic thermal dark matter paradigm, this search offers a way to probe dark sector targets beyond the neutrino floor of dark matter direct detection. This provides an additional compelling motivation for the development of high-energy muon beam infrastructure.

item.title: Precision physics at the muon collider: m_W and CKM matrix elements
item.dc:creator: Ludovica Aperio Bella et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

We examine the potential for a 10~TeV lepton collider to carry out precision measurements of the W boson mass and W boson couplings strength, i.e. the CKM matrix elements. We consider the several W boson production mechanisms and focus on the most copious at 10~TeV, that is effective γW →W, a process viable at both opposite sign and same-sign leptonic colliders. We find that the leptonic W decay channel can hardly be competitive with present determinations, due to lack of rate. The hadronic channel has potential to improve over the current ≃10~MeV from measurements at hadron colliders, motivating detector developments towards high-precision hadronic energy measurements. We find that the precision understanding of the detector response to hadrons can also lead to a determination of the CKM matrix elements. We expect determination of CKM matrix elements surpassing by far the present precision for couplings involving heavy quarks, notably V_cb, avoiding the present bottle-necks due to poor knowledge of hadronic matrix elements needed in low energy extractions of CKM matrix elements. Our findings motivate detector developments towards high-precision hadronic energy measurements and flavor tagging.

item.title: Heavy Vector Triplets at a Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Francesca Acanfora et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

Heavy spin-one particles are well-motivated new physics candidates that can have their origin in weakly coupled extensions of the Standard Model gauge group or in strongly coupled Composite Higgs models. Due to the variety of production and decay modes, heavy vector triplets are a useful benchmark for the study and comparison of future colliders. Here we perform a detailed collider analysis of a variety of 2 →2 and 2 →3 processes at a proposed future muon collider. We focus on decays into leptons and Standard Model gauge bosons, and find that heavy vector triplets could be probed up to masses of around 12TeV for almost any (perturbative) value of the coupling. We compare the direct reach of a muon collider to the LHC and to updated projections for the HL-LHC, HE-LHC and FCC-hh, and include indirect limits from future measurements of electroweak precision observables. We find that a muon collider offers projected sensitivities that are competitive with future hadron colliders, exceeding those of the HE-LHC in the scenarios considered though not reaching the projected sensitivity of the FCC-hh.

item.title: Probing anomalous quartic gauge couplings via vector boson scattering at the same-sign muon collider
item.dc:creator: Lopamudra Mukherjee et al.
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

The measurement of quartic gauge couplings (QGCs) provides a crucial test of the non-Abelian gauge structure of the Standard Model and offers sensitivity to new physics effects. In this work, we explore the potential of the proposed multi-TeV same-sign muon collider, μTRISTAN, to probe anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) through vector boson scattering (VBS) processes. Owing to the same-sign initial state, s-channel contributions are absent, rendering VBS as the dominant production mode and thereby significantly enhancing the sensitivity to aQGCs. Using dimension-8 Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators, we classify the relevant operator sets contributing to charged and neutral QGCs, and confront them with existing bounds from the LHC. A detailed collider analysis is performed across multiple final states: 2V2ν, Vγℓν, 2Vℓν, 2γ2ℓ, and 2V2ℓ (V= reconstructed W and Z boson), applying optimized selection strategies. We present the projected sensitivities at the μTRISTAN with center-of-mass energies 2 TeV and 6 TeV, with integrated luminosities of 1 ab⁻¹ and 10 ab⁻¹, and demonstrate significant improvements over current experimental limits from the LHC. Our results establish μTRISTAN as a powerful probe of electroweak symmetry breaking dynamics and aQGCs in a model-independent framework.

item.title: Probing the Tau Anomalous Magnetic Moment at Colliders: From Ultra-Peripheral Collisions to the Precision Frontier
item.dc:creator: Natascia Vignaroli
item.description:
Watchlist hit (muon collider) — abstract only, not yet read for a briefing.

The anomalous magnetic moment of the tau lepton, a_τ, represents a fundamental test of the Standard Model (SM) and a high-sensitivity probe for New Physics in the third generation of leptons. Due to the tau’s extremely short lifetime, traditional spin-precession measurements remain inaccessible, necessitating innovative experimental strategies at high-energy colliders. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current experimental landscape, highlighting the recent paradigm shift from LEP-era constraints to the unprecedented precision reached at the LHC. These results are critically compared with the latest measurements from proton-proton collisions, including the recent CMS observation of the γγ→ττ process and the ATLAS constraints from the high-mass Drell-Yan tail. We evaluate their complementarity and the challenges related to Effective Field Theory validity at the TeV scale. Finally, we outline the future prospects for a_τ at Belle II and the Future Circular Collider (FCC) stages. While FCC-hh in PbPb mode provides a theoretically clean environment, its sensitivity remains limited to 𝒪(10⁻²⁾. Conversely, the next generation of lepton facilities, specifically Belle II and FCC-ee, aims for the 𝒪(10⁻⁵⁾ level, required to probe SM electroweak loop corrections. We acknowledge that the technology necessary may require humanity to evolve to a Kardashev Level-I or Level-II civilization, which is all the more reason to begin R\&D now.

Under-construction systems at the HL-LHC (CMS MTD, ATLAS HGTD, CMS HGCAL) demonstrate the maturity of 30–50\,ps silicon timing at the million-channel scale. The EIC, LHCb VELO Upgrade~II, and ALICE~3 push this technology into new regimes of radiation hardness, material budget, and granularity. (iv) The Far-future facilities such as the Muon Collider and FCC require a further leap to ∼10\,ps, setting the agenda for the next decade of detector R\&D.
